lines: Thunder shook the brewing stand so hard the bottles clicked like teeth, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked bottles, remedies, and the bell rope after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the brewing stand, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the bottles twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have bottles to set right.
The village has been noisy lately, and not in the harmless market-day way.
I heard about that. Around here, news grows legs before breakfast.
People are pretending they are calm. That usually means they are not.
One event becomes ten versions by sunset. I am trying to remember the first one.
The bell, the gossip, the running feet... It all leaves a mark.
